title: Evaluate Reverse Polish Notation
kidExplanation: Tokens in RPN: numbers wait on a stack; an operator pops two, computes, pushes back.
plainProblem: Evaluate Reverse Polish Notation: Tokens in RPN: numbers wait on a stack; an operator pops two, computes, pushes back. Worked example — input: tokens = ["2","1","+","3","*"]; expected output: 9. Why: (2+1)*3 Interview pattern to name out loud: Stack (last-in, first-out pile).

thinkingSteps.title: Brute force idea
thinkingSteps.body: For “Evaluate Reverse Polish Notation”, first say a correct slow approach: scan or retry every candidate until the example works by hand. Input tokens = ["2","1","+","3","*"] should still produce 9.

thinkingSteps.title: Why it is slow
thinkingSteps.body: Count the nested work. If each choice restarts a full scan, time blows up. Name the cost before optimizing — interviewers want that honesty. Target after the insight: O(n).

thinkingSteps.title: Aha insight
thinkingSteps.body: To evaluate a given reverse Polish notation expression, we can use a stack data structure. We iterate through the tokens in the expression, and for each token, if it is a number, we push it onto the stack. If it is an operator ('+', '-', '*', '/'), we pop the top two elements from the stack, apply the operator to them, and push the result back onto the stack. At the end, the top element of the stack will be the final result of the expression.
